r.b: Q: What happens at a WCQ event?

r: : The SAWCQ is a big, exciting 3-day event that takes place from Friday to Sunday. Duelists from all over will attend these events to compete for exclusive prizes and spend the weekend Dueling, trading, and hanging out with hundreds of other Yu-Gi-Oh! fans. In addition to the invite only Advanced Main Event which will start on June 20
, the SAWCQ will also feature a Genesys Championship and a Dragon Duel Championship.
Click here for details on the Genesys Championship. Note Day 1 of the Genesys Championship will take place on Friday June 19
Click here for details on the Dragon Duel Championship.

In addition to the invite only Advanced Main Event, Genesys Championship, and Dragon Duel Championship, there are numerous Public Events, like Win-A-Mat & More Tournaments (Advanced and Genesys), Speed Duel,
(DUEL LINKS)*,
(MASTER DUEL)*,and Regional Qualifier tournaments. Competitive or casual, there is something for everyone to do at the SAWCQ.
*In order to participate in DUEL LINKS or MASTER DUEL, Duelists will need to have the latest version of the app on your devices.

r.b: Q: Will there be meal breaks during the tournament?

r: As there will be food and drinks available inside the tournament hall, there will not be any meal breaks scheduled into the tournament.

r.b: Q: How many Rounds will the SAWCQ 2026 have?

r: The total number of Duelists will determine the number of Rounds that are played.

r.b: Q: How many Duelists will advance to Day 2?

r: If there are 256 or fewer Duelists registered for the SAWCQ, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 15 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 257 – 512 Duelists registered for the SAWCQ, then the Top 64 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.
If there are 513 – 1024 Duelists registered for the SAWCQ, then the Top 128 Duelists OR Duelists with a minimum of 18 Points, whichever number is larger, will advance to Day 2.

r.b: Q: How many Duelists will advance to the Top Cut?

r: The tournament will cut to Top 8 after all rounds of Swiss are completed.

r.b: Q: Are there entry fees for the SAWCQ?

r: There are no entry fees for the SAWCQ. Championship Series (YCS) events. Last-Chance Qualifiers are offered on Friday June 19

r: All Duelists wishing to compete in SAWCQ 2026 will need to have earned an invite at any of the following
A Regional Qualifier hosted between July 2025 and June 2026
This includes Regional Qualifier single-elimination flights hosted at YCS and Remote Duel YCS events
A Latin America WCQ – National in 2026
A Dragon Duel event hosted between July 2025 and June 2026
OTS Championship event hosted between August 2025 and June 2026
YCS event between August 2025 and June 2026
This includes Remote Duel YCS
This does
include TEAM YCS

Any Dragon Duelist that earned an invite to the SAWCQ, may choose to instead participate in the South America Dragon Duel Championship (SADDC). Aside from the Main Tournaments, anyone wishing to attend the SAWCQ 2026 to spectate or take part in any of the Public Events or attractions does not need an invite to do that as the hall is open to the public and all are welcome.

r.b: Q: What is the SAWQP Playoff and how do I qualify to play in it?

r: Throughout the course of the 2025-2026 Organized Play season, Duelists have been earning World Qualifying Points by competing at Regional Qualifiers, Latin America WCQ – National, Dragon Duels, OTS Championships, and at the Yu-Gi-Oh! Championship Series. Whenever a Duelist places high enough in those events to earn an invite to the WCQ, they earn World Qualifying Points based on their standing.
On Friday, June 19
at the SAWCQ, the

Points earners from the 2025-2026 Organized Play season in Central America, based on the chart below are eligible to register for this special playoff tournament. Eligible Duelists can check in and register for the World Qualifying Points Playoff between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM. The event is scheduled to begin at 10:30 AM

You can find the Top Points earners for the 2025-2026 Organized Play season here:
https://www.yugioh-card.com/en/events/wqp
A total of 16 Duelists will compete in the World Qualifying Playoff. See the charts below for the breakdown:

r.b: Deck Lists will be required when you register for the SAWQP. Registration will be online, and your Deck List must be submitted online. You can prepare your Deck Lists ahead of time at https://registration.yugioh-card.com/ to have them ready when you register.

r: Eligible Duelists must be present to claim their spot to compete. If any of the Top Points earners are not present to play, the Playoff spot will then be given to the next ranked Duelist based on the country breakdown above. For example, if only 1 Duelist from Colombia is missing from the Top 16 Duelists then the next Duelist in line to compete will be the third place Duelist from Colombia’s leaderboard. Same example will apply for any other leaderboard. Duelists must register and be present no later than 10:00 AM in order to be called if there is an open spot. We encourage any of the Top Points earners from the 2025-2026 season to check in between 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM so that we can quickly fill any open spots if needed.

The 16 Duelists from the 2025-2026 season who attend the SAWCQ and register and claim their spot for the SAWQP, based on the chart above will then play in an Advanced Constructed, Single-Elimination Tournament. The winner of the Playoff will win an invite to the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG World Championship 2026.
Here is a link to the World Qualifying Points FAQ for further information:

r.b: South America Genesys Championship (SAGC) Event and Registration Information

and Sunday June 21

Swiss Rounds followed by a Single-Elimination Playoff Top Cut. Rounds are dependent on the total number of Duelists at the time registration closes.
Time Limit: 50 Minutes per Swiss Round.
Genesys rules are simple:
No Link Monsters or Pendulum Monsters are allowed. All other cards are allowed. The original field layout is used, with no Extra Monster Zones nor Pendulum Zones.
The standard Forbidden & Limited Cards list is not used. All those cards can be used, except Link Monsters and Pendulum Monsters. Usual limit of 3 copies max of any card still applies.

Deck construction uses a point system. Some cards are assigned a point value; most cards cost zero points. The total point cost of cards in your Main Deck, Extra Deck, and Side Deck (combined) cannot exceed the point cap for that event.

For the Genesys Championship, we will use the 100 Points cap for Deck-building. Click the link below for the current Genesys Points list. Conversely, you can build your Deck using NEURON, the Yu-Gi-Oh! TCG support app.
Yu-Gi-Oh! GENESYS – Yu-Gi-Oh! TRADING CARD GAME
